h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר מ״ב Pesach — Maamar Mem Bais

p: בַּגְּמָרָא
In the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים ק"כ.):
(Pesachim 120a):
שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ — מַה שְּׁבִיעִי רְשׁוּת אַף שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים רְשׁוּת וְכוּלֵּי.

"'Six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day shall be an assembly to Hashem your God, etc.'—just as on the seventh day eating matzah is optional, so too on all six days it is optional, etc."
וְלָמָּה נִרְמַז זֶה שֶׁמַּצָּה כָּל שִׁשָּׁה רְשׁוּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, וְלֹא בְּיוֹם אַחֵר?
Now why was this law—that matzah is optional on all six days—alluded to specifically through the seventh day, and not through any other day?

אַךְ בִּפְשׁוּטוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא רְבוּתָא, שֶׁאַף בַּשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חוֹבָה לֶאֱכוֹל פַּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֲכִילַת מַצָּה רְשׁוּת, שֶׁיּוֹצֵא בְּמַצָּה עֲשִׁירָה רַק שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה חָמֵץ, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בְּחוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד שֶׁאֵין חוֹבָה כְּלָל לֶאֱכוֹל פַּת.

Simply, one can say it is a greater novelty: that even on the seventh day, when there is a positive obligation to eat bread because it is Yom Tov, nevertheless eating regular matzah is optional—since one fulfills the meal requirement with enriched matzah (matzah ashirah) so long as it is not chametz—and all the more so on Chol HaMoed when there is no obligation to eat bread at all.
אֲבָל הָעִנְיָן: דְּעִיקַּר מִצְוַת מַצָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶחֶם עֹנִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
However, the deeper explanation is that the essence of the mitzvah of matzah is that it be "bread of poverty (oni)," as it is said
(דְּבָרִים ט"ז, ג'):
(Devarim 16:3):
שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי
"Seven days you shall eat matzos upon it, bread of poverty"
דְּעִנְיַן מִצְוַת פֶּסַח הוּא שֶׁמִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹמֵד עַל הַפֶּתַח, וְהוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ לְעֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו,

for the essence of the Pesach offering is that it becomes crystal clear that Hashem, may He be blessed, stands at the doorway, and it is overtly revealed to the eyes of Israel that the King of kings stands over them,
וּמִזֶּה יָכוֹל הָאָדָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהַשִּׂיג גַּאֲוָה.
and from such exalted privilege a person might, God forbid, fall into pride.
וְאִיתָא
And it is stated
(חוּלִּין פ"ט.):
(Chullin 89a):
חוֹשְׁקַנִי בָּכֶם שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֲנִי מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָכֶם גְּדוּלָּה אַתֶּם מְמַעֲטִין עַצְמְכֶם לְפָנַי: נָתַתִּי גְּדוּלָּה לְאַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי
"I desire you because even at the moment I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me: I gave greatness to Avraham, etc."
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁאֵין הַמְכוּוָן עַל גְּדוּלַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁזֶּה לֹא נֶחְשָׁב כְּלוּם אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, רַק הַמְכוּוָן כְּשֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹר;

and we have already explained that this does not refer to worldly greatness—which meant nothing at all to our father Avraham, peace be upon him—rather it refers to when Hashem, may He be blessed, bestows spiritual light;
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה הַתְחָלַת הָאוֹר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
for our father Avraham, peace be upon him, who was the beginning of the light, as they said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ב', ג'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 2:3):
יְהִי אוֹר — זֶה אַבְרָהָם,
"'Let there be light'—this is Avraham,"
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה לוֹ אוֹר ה' אָמַר: אָנֹכִי עָפָר וָאֵפֶר;
when the light of Hashem was revealed to him he said, "I am dust and ashes";
וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁזָּכוּ לְכָל אוֹר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תּוֹרָה אוֹר, אָמְרוּ: נַחְנוּ מָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and Moshe and Aharon, who merited the entire light of the words of Torah—"Torah is light"—said, "What are we?", as they said
(שָׁם בְּחוּלִּין):
(ibid. in Chullin):
גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי.
"What is said of Moshe and Aharon is even greater than what is said of Avraham, etc."

וְעַל זֶה בָּא הַמִּצְוָה: לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ—שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְבַעֵר הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה מִכֹּל וָכֹל מִלֵּב—שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי, שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְמַעֲטִין עַצְמָם וְלֹא יִתְגָּאוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל יְדֵי מַעֲלַת הַקְרָבַת הַפֶּסַח,

Therefore came the commandment "You shall not eat chametz upon it"—meaning one must utterly eradicate the leaven in the dough [pride] from the heart—"seven days you shall eat matzos upon it, bread of poverty," so that through this they merit to diminish themselves and not grow haughty, God forbid, from the lofty stature of offering the Pesach sacrifice,
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and so wrote the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' קנ"ז.):
לֶחֶם עֹנִי — מַאן דָּא? דָּוִד מַלְכָּא, דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ
"'Bread of poverty'—who is this? King David, of whom it is written
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ו, א'):
(Tehillim 86:1):
כִּי עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אָנִי.
'For I am poor and needy.'"
וְאִם כֵּן בַּשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁזָּכוּ אָז יִשְׂרָאֵל: רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאוּ נְבִיאִים וִיחֶזְקֵאל
Now, if so, on the seventh day, when Israel merited "A maidservant saw at the Sea what prophets and Yechezkel did not see"
(מְכִילְתָּא הַשִּׁירָה ג' וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב' ס"ד:),
(Mechilta Shirah 3 and holy Zohar, Vol. 2, 64b),
וִיכוֹלִים מִזֶּה לְהַשִּׂיג גַּאֲוָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וְאָז הָיוּ מְאַבְּדִין הַכֹּל, וְאִם כֵּן הָיָה מֵהָרָאוּי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בַּשְּׁבִיעִי אֲכִילַת מַצָּה חוֹבָה
they could easily fall into pride from such vision, God forbid, and thereby forfeit everything, so by right eating matzah should have been strictly mandatory on the seventh day
וְלִימְּדָנוּ הַכָּתוּב שֶׁאַף בַּשְּׁבִיעִי רְשׁוּת:
yet Scripture teaches us that even on the seventh day it is optional:
דְּכֵיוָן דִּכְבָר זָכוּ בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶחֶם עֹנִי, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּדַע הָאָדָם שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה לֶחֶם עֹנִי

because once they already merited on the first night to internalize "bread of poverty"—meaning a person knows that everything comes from Hashem, may He be blessed, which is what "bread of poverty" signifies
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
along the lines of what is brought in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן י"ג):
(Tikkun 13):
מַצָּה פְּרוּסָה ד', מַצָּה שְׁלֵימָה ה'
"A broken matzah is Dalet, a whole matzah is Hei"

וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּת, סִיהֲרָא דְּלֵית לַהּ מִגַּרְמָא כְּלוּם, וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת אָמַר: כִּי עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אָנֹכִי, תּוֹלַעַת וְלֹא אִישׁ

which is the attribute of Malchus, the moon that has nothing of its own, just as King David, peace be upon him, who was a chariot for Malchus, declared, "For I am poor and needy," "a worm and not a man"
וְשׁוּב מוֹעִיל זֶה עַל כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים, רַק שֶׁיִּשְׁמוֹר אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִשְּׂאוֹר וְחָמֵץ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִכְנוֹס שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה;
that illumination then suffices for all seven days, provided one guards oneself from leaven and chametz so that the leaven in the dough [pride] does not enter;

וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאֲכִילַת מַצָּה בַּשְּׁבִיעִי רְשׁוּת, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בִּשְׁאָר יָמִים, וְנִלְמַד בְּמִדַּת "דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל", וְרַק "בָּעֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ מַצֹּת" הַכָּתוּב קְבָעוֹ חוֹבָה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ מִצְוָה גַּם בִּשְׁאָר הַיָּמִים בְּמַצָּה

and since eating matzah on the seventh day is optional, all the more so on the other days, as derived via the rule of "anything that was included in a general statement," and only "in the evening you shall eat matzos" did Scripture establish as a strict obligation, though there is still a positive mitzvah to eat matzah on the other days as well
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמַאֲמָר ט"ז).
(as explained in Maamar 16).

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 120a — "'Six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day shall be an assembly to Hashem your God': just as the seventh day is optional, so too the six days are optional." Rashbam (who comments on this chapter in place of Rashi): the seventh day left the general rule to teach about the whole rule; one may eat meat without bread on those days, or even fast.

When the Holy One, blessed is He, wished to bring them near to Him, He gave them the place of 'bread of poverty' — lechem oni is written. Who is the poor one (oni)? This is King David, of whom it is written, 'For I am poor and needy' (Tehillim 86:1)."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13 (28b) — "Why was it a broken matzah? Because its vav, its 'leg,' was taken from it to be in the mitzvah (מצוה), and the broken matzah remained a dalet. Therefore the broken matzah is dalet, the whole matzah is hei. And therefore we say whole Hallel and half Hallel on Pesach, corresponding to the whole matzah and the broken matzah."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 9 — “And matzah, ‘bread of poverty,’ corresponds to the Dalet, from the word dalus, poverty, for Knesses Yisrael are poor and needy, having nothing but what Hashem bestows on them, for they count by the moon, which has nothing of its own. And this is the opposite of chametz, the leaven in the dough, which raises the dough: the root of the inclination toward haughtiness. Matzah is ‘the food of healing,’ and as long as one is engaged in a cure, the harmful thing must not be found; and the seven days of Pesach they were still engaged in the cure, for on the seventh day the Egyptians again pursued them.” Connection: The same pairing of “bread of poverty” with the moon that has nothing of its own against the haughtiness of leaven; it adds why the cure must last through the seventh day.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Pesach 5631 — “‘This matzah… because the dough of our fathers had no time to leaven before the King of kings revealed Himself’: the Rav explained in his Siddur that matzah is as it is, without self-elevation, whereas chametz is the coarseness that lifts itself up and swells; and because they had a revelation of the Shechinah, it remained matzah. So too in the Zohar, Pinchas: the difference between chametz and matzah is a single point, between hei and ches. For hei is the point within the dalet, which knows that it has nothing but the inner point that Hashem gave; and when one draws that point to himself, it becomes ches, and that is chametz.” Connection: The Sefas Emes likewise ties matzah to the self-effacement of Malchus, the dalet that has nothing of its own, before revelation, and adds the mechanism of pride: claiming the God-given point as one's own turns matzah into chametz.

p: וְנִכְתַּב רֶמֶז זֶה בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ.
And this allusion is written in the phrase "And on the seventh day shall be an assembly to Hashem your God."
וּכְבָר שָׁאֲלוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
Now they already asked in the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים ס"ח:):
(Pesachim 68b):
כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: עֲצֶרֶת תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם, וְנֶחְלְקוּ בָּזֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
"One verse states 'an assembly to Hashem your God' and one verse states 'an assembly shall it be to you,' over which Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disputed."
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גַּם הַ"לָּכֶם", שֶׁהוּא הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ
And we have already explained that all agree there must also be the "to you" aspect—meaning bodily enjoyment sanctified so that it becomes "an assembly to Hashem your God"

אַךְ הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה' אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם, לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם: שֶׁמִּי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִהְיוֹת אֶצְלוֹ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם, וּמִי שֶׁקָּשֶׁה עָלָיו זֶה יִהְיֶה כּוּלּוֹ לַה', וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּמַה שֶּׁהוּא לַה' צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן לָכֶם,

except that the dispute is that Rabbi Eliezer holds it should be either "all to Hashem" or "all to you" depending on the individual's spiritual stature: one who can elevate bodily pleasure into holiness ("to Hashem your God") should devote it "all to you," whereas one for whom that is difficult should devote it "all to Hashem"—though even in what is "to Hashem" there must also be a "to you" dimension,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִלּוּבְּלִין זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה עַל אֶחָד בְּיָמָיו שֶׁהָיָה בַּעַל בָּשָׂר אַף שֶׁהָיָה עָנִי אַךְ הָיָה מַתְמִיד גָּדוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה, וְאָמַר שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג תַּעֲנוּג וּבְרִיאוּת הַגּוּף מֵהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;

just as our holy master [the Chozeh] of Lublin, may his righteous and holy memory be for a blessing, remarked about someone in his days who was stout despite being poor because he was a tremendous Torah scholar, saying that he derived physical pleasure and bodily health from words of Torah;
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סוֹבֵר: חַלְּקֵהוּ, חֶצְיוֹ לַאֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וְחֶצְיוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵיגוֹת הָעֲבוֹדָה.
whereas Rabbi Yehoshua holds: "Divide it—half for eating and drinking, and half for the study hall," requiring both modes of service.
אַךְ לָמָּה נִכְתַּב בִּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת "עֲצֶרֶת תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם", וּבְפֶסַח כְּתִיב "לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ"? הֲוָה לֵיהּ לִכְתּוֹב שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד!
Yet why is "an assembly shall it be to you" written regarding Shemini Atzeres, while regarding Pesach it is written "to Hashem your God"? It could have written both in the same place!
אַךְ הָעֵסֶק בְּפֶסַח הוּא לְבָרֵר הָאֲכִילוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, וְלִימְּדָנוּ הַכָּתוּב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אַף "לָכֶם", הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף, "עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ", לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם;

Because the central work of Pesach is to refine physical eating so that it is in holiness, so Scripture teaches that even the "to you" aspect—bodily enjoyment—must be "an assembly to Hashem your God," for the sake of Heaven;
וּבִשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת הָעֵסֶק מִקּוֹדֶם לְמֵיתַב בְּצִילָא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא דְּהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת נְבִיעֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
whereas on Shemini Atzeres the preceding spiritual work was sitting in the Shade of Faith [the Sukkah], which is words of Torah, and Shemini Atzeres is the wellspring of Torah
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת),
(as explained in Shemini Atzeres),
וְנִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גַּם "לָכֶם", שֶׁגַּם הַגּוּף יֵהָנֶה מֵהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְיִהְיֶה לוֹ קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים מֵהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּאָמוּר.
so it is written in the Torah that words of Torah must also be "to you," meaning even the physical body should derive delight and life-sustenance from words of Torah, as stated.

וְאָמַר הַכָּתוּב שֶׁאַף בַּשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁזּוֹכִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה—"עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ"—וּמִזֶּה יְכוֹלִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהִתְגָּאוֹת וּלְאַבֵּד הַכֹּל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם אָז אֲכִילַת מַצָּה רְשׁוּת, שֶׁכְּבָר הוֹעִיל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה דְּלַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג אָדָם מַדְרֵיגָה זוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶחֶם עֹנִי, שֶׁיֵּדַע דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם.

And Scripture states that even on the seventh day, when one merits that bodily pleasure is sanctified—"an assembly to Hashem your God"—from which one might, God forbid, become proud and lose everything, nevertheless even then eating matzah is optional, because the matzah eaten on the first night has already enabled a person to attain the level of "bread of poverty," knowing that he possesses nothing of his own.

וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהָיָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, שֶׁהָיָה הַפֶּסַח קָרֵב וְנֶאֱכָל בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וּמִפְּנֵי קְדוּשַׁת הַפֶּסַח שֶׁלֹּא יַכְנִיס גַּאֲוָה בַּלֵּב נִצְטַוִּינוּ: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי—נִקְרָא הֶחָג עַל שֵׁם הַמַּצּוֹת שֶׁנּוֹהֵג כָּל שִׁבְעָה;

Now when the Holy Temple stood, when the Pesach offering was sacrificed and eaten on the first night, and because of the holiness of the Pesach offering—so that it would not instill pride in the heart—we were commanded "seven days you shall eat matzos upon it, bread of poverty," the festival was called [in the Torah] after the matzos, which applies all seven days;

וְאַחַר הַחוּרְבָּן שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ פֶּסַח, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹפִיעַ קְדוּשַׁת הַפֶּסַח אַף בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה—וְהַיְינוּ פֶּסַח דִּלְעָתִיד שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹמֵד עַל הַפֶּתַח וּמְפוֹרָשׁ נֶגֶד עַיִן, וּבִזְמַן הַזֶּה אֵין הֶבְדֵּל בְּפוֹעַל בֵּין לֵיל רִאשׁוֹן לִשְׁאָר הַיָּמִים—נִקְרָא הֶחָג בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים "חַג הַפֶּסַח" עַל שֵׁם קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ בְּכָל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים.

whereas after the destruction, when we have no physical Pesach offering, yet the holiness of Pesach still shines even nowadays—referring to the future Pesach when it will be clarified before all eyes that Hashem, may He be blessed, stands at the doorway, and nowadays there is no practical difference between the first night and the remaining days—the festival is called in the parlance of the Sages "the Festival of Pesach," after its holiness which shines throughout all seven days.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 68b — "One verse says, 'an assembly to Hashem your God,' and one verse says, 'an assembly shall it be to you.' Rabbi Eliezer holds: either all of it for Hashem or all of it for you; Rabbi Yehoshua holds: divide it — half for Hashem and half for you." The Gemara continues: all agree that on Atzeres (Shavuos) "for you" is also needed. Rashi: that one rejoices on it with food and drink.
